title: Foundation 1: prove source-obligation identity and discharge on five real procedures
description:
THE FIRST SUCCESSOR. No other foundation may be designed in implementation detail
until this stabilises.

PREMISE CHANGE (why this exists): PRs #475/#476/#477 reached DESIGN_INVALIDATED
after repeatedly producing NEW defect classes following material contract changes
and fresh full reviews. The shared root cause was not implementation quality: in
all three, unsettled concepts were GENERALIZED ACROSS THE CORPUS before their
trust boundaries had been proven by a small number of concrete
source-to-execution examples. Successor work inverts that order.

GOAL: prove the disputed trust boundary — that an authoritative source obligation
can be created INDEPENDENTLY OF THE PROJECTOR and discharged by exact projected
atoms — on a SMALL VERTICAL SLICE of real SRD procedures. Do NOT design a
universal clause taxonomy. PR #475 is a design spike, not an accepted IR.

REQUIRED PROOF SET (five real, source-backed procedures):
  1. a compound save / damage / duration / repeat / termination procedure;
  2. a mutually exclusive attack or damage-mode procedure;
  3. an option-local feature whose mechanics must NOT be hoisted to its parent;
  4. a lifecycle or resource procedure;
  5. a deliberately model-adjudicated or source-ambiguous boundary.

ACCEPTANCE — each of the five must demonstrate:
  * the obligation is produced INDEPENDENTLY of the projector (the producer of
    an artifact can never define the standard its own output is judged by);
  * exact source identity and locator;
  * the required semantic facets;
  * the exact projected atom or branch identities that discharge it;
  * multiplicity — one atom cannot discharge two distinct obligations;
  * option or branch locality;
  * fail-closed handling of a missing facet;
  * provider-neutral execution against a REAL generated pack record, for the
    cases where the clause is a direct engine input.

EXPLICIT NON-GOALS: no universal obligation identity, no contract-composition
framework, no aggregate closure, no registry authority generalisation, no
corpus-wide taxonomy. Those consume this and are blocked on it.

SALVAGE INPUT from PR #475 (design input only, not code to extend): the ADR
reasoning about clause-level completeness; the CAPTURED / PROJECTED / SUPPORTED /
DISCOVERABLE separation; structured failure vocabulary; cardinality and
fail-closed predicates; the adversarial test cases; and the worked examples
showing why projector-authored obligations are unsafe.
acceptance_criteria:
• Five real source-backed procedures, covering compound save/damage/duration/repeat/termination, mutually exclusive damage modes, option-local mechanics, lifecycle or resource, and a model-adjudicated boundary.
• For each: obligation produced independently of the projector, with exact source identity and locator, required facets, and the exact projected atom or branch identities that discharge it.
• Multiplicity enforced so one atom cannot discharge two obligations; option and branch locality preserved.
• A missing facet fails closed.
• Provider-neutral execution against a real generated pack record wherever the clause is a direct engine input.
• No universal taxonomy, registry authority, or aggregate closure is introduced.

CORE DESIGN DECISIONS (falsifiable, see packet):
 * N3 ONE OBLIGATION = ONE FACET OCCURRENCE, with `ordinal` IN the identity.
   Supersedes #475 one-obligation-per-clause, which merely relocates multiplicity
   into clause decomposition. W1's two identical Con saves are the proof.
 * ObligationId = obl/<digest8>/p<page>/q<quoteHash8>/<facetSlot>/<ordinal>.
   Contains NO record key -> survives the pack omitting the clause entirely.
 * REJECT obl:::<sourceRef>::<locator>::<facet> (#475/#477) on independent grounds:
   no multiplicity discriminator. In #476 it is minted from an AUDIT FINDING ID.
 * REJECT ObligationSource.get()->|undefined (#475): a lookup that can return
   undefined IS the five-occurrence fail-open idiom. Ledger is load-or-throw + iterate.
 * N4 DISCHARGE IS A BIPARTITE MATCHING (Hopcroft-Karp), perfect on the obligation
   side, injective into atoms. Multiplicity becomes structural, not a remembered rule.
 * N5 LOCALITY IS JSON-POINTER CONTAINMENT. AtomId = atom/<recordKey>/<jsonPointer>.
   A projector cannot assert scope it does not have. Answers the handoff's
   "can option locality be expressed without a scope/closure layer?" -> YES.
 * P AUTHORS NO DISCHARGE LINKS AT ALL. E computes the matching. A projector that
   cannot state a claim cannot state a weak one.
 * Owner binding computed by E from (sourcePage, verbatim source heading) ->
   unique record; fail closed on 0 or >=2. All five cases resolve uniquely.
 * N7 evaluate(): Result<Report, Fatal>. Report.ok is a DERIVED GETTER. Empty ledger
   is Fatal. N8 no free-text field is ever a validation target.
 * N9 adjudication fails closed BOTH ways (ADJUDICATION_MISSING /
   ADJUDICATION_SILENTLY_DETERMINIZED / DETERMINISTIC_DISCHARGED_BY_ADJUDICATION).
 * N10 READINESS IS COMPUTED, NEVER STORED. Five dimensions, not four:
   CAPTURED / PROJECTED / ENGINE-SUPPORTED / DISCOVERABLE / REFERENCE-EXECUTED.
 * POSITIVE ABSENCE = anchored obligation exists in frozen source + owner record
   resolved + EXHAUSTIVE walk of record.data yields no match. Plus a BOUNDED
   PageCensus over X(F) for exactly the five proof pages, residual MUST be empty.
   No sentinel, no text search, no closed schema over RulesRecord.data (it is `unknown`).

=== F1 DESIGN R2 (REVIEW ROUND 1 RESPONSE) 2026-07-28 -- design-only, nothing implemented ===
R1 was directionally accepted but NOT approved. Ten blockers addressed; R1 is superseded
by R2 wherever they disagree.

CORRECTIONS TO R1 (each was a real error, not a refinement):
 1. TRUST MODEL WAS DISHONEST. R1 claimed the curator is "trusted for nothing" while the
    evaluator consumes curator-authored facets, classification, multiplicity, locality and
    non-mechanical exclusions. R2: anchoring proves SOURCE IDENTITY AND DRIFT ONLY, never
    interpretation. A BOUNDED, INDEPENDENTLY REVIEWED contract is the semantic authority
    for F1, sealed by contractHash = sha256(RFC-8785 JCS(contract \ {review,contractHash})).
    E and R accept ONLY APPROVED_CONTRACT_HASH -> editing the ledger cannot silently change
    what F1 proves. Nine numbered items the reviewer must inspect per procedure are listed.
    CORPUS COMPLETENESS IS EXPLICITLY NOT CLAIMED.
 2. SINGLE-QUOTE-HASH GROUPING WAS WRONG. W2 and W4 are genuinely multi-anchor. R2 adds
    Procedure{ownerAnchor, supportingAnchors[], crossReferences[]} with AnchorRole
    (semantic-owner | general-rule | value-table | scaling-table | continuation) and
    Obligation.derivedFrom[]. derivedFrom.length>1 without a CrossReference is fatal.
    VERIFIED IN-TREE: Longsword p.66 table row + Versatile definition p.65 (which lives in
    rule:weapon-properties, locator "pp. 64, 65", as ONE concatenated data.text blob -> the
    supporting anchor has NO addressable evidence today). Font of Magic p.43 + table:
    the-sorcerer p.42 Sorcery Points column + table:creating-spell-slots p.43; the record's
    tableRefs names ONLY creating-spell-slots, so the scaling anchor is unreachable.
    EDGE CASE the reviewer must confirm: table:the-sorcerer row "1st" has an EMPTY STRING in
    the Sorcery Points column (no pool before level 2).
 3. "EXACT BYTE RANGE OF THE FROZEN SOURCE" WAS FALSE -- pdfjs/pdftotext yield text, not PDF
    byte offsets. R2 makes NO PDF byte-range claim. CanonicalSource{pdfDigest, extractorId,
    extractorVersion, canonicalTextDigest}; SpanLocator{canonicalTextDigest,page,regionId,
    startOffset,endOffset,spanHash}. Text-unit census replaced by SPAN TILING over bounded
    proof regions: spans must tile exactly (UNCOVERED_RANGE / OVERLAPPING_SPANS are fatal),
    each classified once as obligation-bearing | connective (MUST name its obligations) |
    structure | non-mechanical | excluded-from-proof.
 4. atomsOf() CONFLATED ENUMERATION WITH INTERPRETATION. R2 splits three layers: exhaustive
    RawNodeIndex (mechanical); evaluator-owned EvidenceUnit extraction (closed shape set,
    importer may not define shapes); candidates naming every consumed pointer. KEY DEVICE:
    each unit splits consumedPointers into DISCRIMINANT (injective, at most one unit) and
    SHARED (reusable, declared statically per shape). This is what lets Longsword's two
    mode-local damage units legitimately share /damageType while Burnt Othur's single
    /mechanics/saves/0 still collapses. Unconsumed nodes in declared fail-closed subtrees ->
    UNSUPPORTED_PROJECTION_SHAPE, never "absent".
 5. exclusiveModes WAS OVERLOADED AND IS REMOVED. 22 case-specific facets replace it.
    Longsword = operationalModeSelector (exactly one ACTIVE mode at runtime) + two
    modeLocalDamage -- NOT an exclusion partition. Fighting Style = choiceCardinality +
    duplicateSelectionProhibited + six optionLocalEffect; R1's "exclusion partition" framing
    is WITHDRAWN (the SRD asserts selection cardinality and a no-repeat rule, not pairwise
    exclusivity). ACCURACY CORRECTION: data.choices[0].choose === 1 IS ALREADY CORRECT, so
    that obligation DISCHARGES TODAY -- the first demonstrated partial success. Font of Magic
    = pool + level-indexed bound + two conversionRelations + assetCreation + termination.
    Wish NARROWED: adjudicationBoundary + conditionalTrigger + recurringDamageOnEvent +
    damageModificationProhibited + attributeOverride + recoveryProcedure +
    probabilisticStateTransition (NOT a resource op). The spell-duplication clause and the
    five bulleted effects are marked excluded-from-proof (they need the spell corpus).
 6. REAL-PACK EXECUTION CONTRADICTION RESOLVED by two stages. STAGE A (pack unchanged):
    anchors resolve, exact failure-identity sets, harness returns ExecutionRefused and never
    fills a gap. STAGE B (minimum end-to-end proof): bounded importer changes to EXACTLY SIX
    record keys -- the five proof records plus rule:weapon-properties -- plus kindSchemas
    validators, so the SAME evaluator reports full discharge and the GENERIC harness executes
    from the real regenerated records. Change-scope guard asserts the six KEYS as an identity
    set. contractHash must be byte-identical before and after Stage B (Stage B may not add
    obligations; if the contract was wrong that is a RE-REVIEW). R1's RC12 ("F1 changes no
    file under packages/core/data or kindSchemas.ts") is WITHDRAWN -> RC12'.
 7. ANTI-HARDCODING IS NOW STRUCTURAL, not a promise. R does not receive a RulesRecord; it
    receives RedactedRecord{data, opaqueId} -- key, name, source, provenance, license are
    ABSENT FROM THE TYPE, and no ProcedureId/ObligationId/ledger is passed. Hardcoding is
    unrepresentable. Tests: rekey/rename -> identical trace; synthetic same-shape record ->
    same behaviour; required field removed -> ExecutionRefused with no fallback; cross-case
    isolation; value-provenance (mutate dc 13->17, trace must follow).
 8. ADJUDICATION BINDS ON STRUCTURE, NOT PROSE: boundaryId + adjudicator, never question
    text. RECONCILIATION of R1's "no relation may originate from the projector": the
    projector MAY PROPOSE a discharge claim (a pointer), it may NEVER DEFINE the obligation
    or its requirements. For deterministic obligations E computes the matching and ignores
    any claim. For adjudication boundaries an explicit structured back-reference is REQUIRED,
    because absence of mechanics is otherwise indistinguishable from omission. An
    unverifiable claim is FALSE_DISCHARGE_CLAIM. Role is provider-neutral 'dm-adjudicator'.
 9. IDENTITIES: full 64-hex sha256 everywhere; truncation is display-only. ProcedureId
    derives from the OWNER ANCHOR ONLY so correcting a supporting anchor does not renumber
    obligations. EvidenceId hashes the SORTED DISCRIMINANT POINTER SET so multi-pointer
    evidence has one stable identity. Stability table: projection change / repair / rekey do
    NOT move obligations; contract edit, extractorVersion bump, or PDF change DO invalidate,
    deliberately, via a reviewed LedgerMigration -- never a silent automatic remap.
10. REVIEWER DECISIONS RECORDED: one obligation per semantic facet occurrence ACCEPTED with
    relation/constraint obligations first-class; bounded human-curated authority ACCEPTED
    after independent review; page+heading owner resolution ACCEPTED for bounded F1 only;
    F2 must MOVE membership fields ENTIRELY TO F3 (not reserve empty fields); current
    data.executionReadiness is a NON-AUTHORITATIVE PROJECTION CLAIM; all five cases retained;
    no redundant direct dependency edges (so 19.4.2/.3/.4 keep transitive ordering via
    19.1.2 -- D2 CLOSED, no edge added); 19.1.7 -> 19.1.1 to be removed ONCE 19.1.1 IS
    FORMALLY MARKED SUPERSEDED (precondition unmet; NOT executed this session -- see Q8).

=== F1 DESIGN R3 (REVIEW ROUND 2 RESPONSE) 2026-07-28 -- design-only, nothing implemented ===
R2 ACCEPTED except the seven corrections below. R3 is the final delta; F1 is now design-
stable pending the external review checkpoint.

1. FREE-TEXT CROSS-REFERENCE EVIDENCE REMOVED. CrossReference.sourceEvidence: string is
   gone. Replaced by CrossReference.evidenceSpan: SpanLocator, which must re-derive from
   the canonical extracted source, lie inside an APPROVED proof region, establish the
   stated link, and participate in contract hashing and review. Human reasoning survives
   as CrossReference.note, which GATES NOTHING (N8). A span may be classified 'connective'
   in the region tiling AND be referenced as cross-reference evidence -- referencing is not
   a second classification, so exactly-once tiling is not violated.
2. EXECUTION HASH GATE SEPARATED FROM REVIEW APPROVAL. APPROVED_CONTRACT_HASH prevents
   implementation running against unreviewed BYTES; it does NOT prove review occurred (a
   developer can edit the constant). Authoritative approval is an EXTERNAL
   eshyra-review-checkpoint binding {reviewedHeadSha, contractHash, procedureIds[],
   reviewerRole, result, implementationPermission}. F1 CONSUMES it and fails closed
   without it: REVIEW_CHECKPOINT_MISSING / _CONTRACT_MISMATCH / _SCOPE_GAP /
   _PERMISSION_DENIED / _HEAD_DRIFT. F1 does NOT build the mechanism.
3. SEMANTIC REVISION IDENTITY ADDED. ObligationId stays stable; a normalized revisionHash
   is added over {facet, locality, classification, sorted derivedFrom, sorted relation
   endpoints}. Procedure and Relation get their own. TWO-TIER RULE: contractHash is
   BYTE-level (any edit, including rationale, forces re-review); revisionHash is SEMANTIC
   (only it invalidates downstream snapshots). Stable ID alone for durable cross-foundation
   references; {id, revisionHash} for anything CACHING OR ASSERTING semantic content
   (baseline fixtures, F3 membership, F4 probes) -> stale pair is OBLIGATION_REVISION_DRIFT.
   PROJECTION REPAIR CHANGES NO revisionHash (nothing projection-derived is hashed).
4. DETERMINISTIC-EXCLUSION ESCAPE HATCH REMOVED. SpanClass 'excluded-from-proof' is
   DELETED. Regions bound the SUBJECT; unrelated surrounding text is simply not in a region.
   Inside a region, deterministic material must be represented or classified
   'unrepresented-deterministic{reason, owner: BeadRef}', which is BLOCKING:
   PROCEDURE_INCOMPLETE, and the procedure CANNOT PASS. W5 RENAMED to "Wish nonstandard-
   effect adjudication and stress-consequence subprocedure" and re-bounded to two p.193
   regions (the GM-latitude paragraph; the stress-consequence paragraph). The basic-use
   clause and five bulleted effects are OUTSIDE both regions, so no exclusion hatch is used
   and NO CLAIM of complete Wish coverage is made.
   CONSEQUENCE that had to be solved: exhaustive raw-node enumeration on spell:wish would
   otherwise flag mechanics.duration/concentration/spellAttack as UNSUPPORTED_PROJECTION_
   SHAPE. Fixed by a reviewed per-procedure subjectPointerScope (pointer prefixes); nodes
   outside it are OUT_OF_SUBJECT (info), inside-but-unconsumed remain fail-closed.
5. opaqueId REMOVED FROM THE HARNESS INPUT. RedactedRecord is now {data} only. The
   correlation token moved OUT of the record into TraceContext, unreachable from semantic
   dispatch, freshly random per execution, pass-through only, randomized in tests, and
   asserted not to affect results.
6. IMPLEMENTATION SPLIT INTO TWO MERGE-BOUND STAGES. F1-A (authority + baseline detection:
   canonical extraction, contract+hash+checkpoint consumer, regions, raw nodes, evidence
   model, evaluator, exact baseline failures, REFUSING harness) changes NO importer output
   and NO generated record, and MUST MERGE BEFORE F1-B STARTS. F1-B (bounded completed
   vertical) may not change the F1-A contract hash or semantics -- if it must, F1-B STOPS
   and F1-A goes back for a new review. Addressable Versatile support in
   rule:weapon-properties is a SEPARATE prerequisite child (F1-B0), additive only.
   SEQUENCING: U5 raw-node enumeration MAY proceed parallel to contract review; U6 semantic
   evidence extraction MUST WAIT for U4's approved contract; F1-B waits for merged F1-A.
   NO IMPLEMENTATION CHILDREN CREATED -- decomposition proposed for approval only.
7. FINAL REVIEWER DECISIONS RECORDED: primary reviewer is the project's independent primary
   reviewer; approval granularity is per-procedure review PLUS integrated full-contract-hash
   approval; the exact CHANGED-RECORD IDENTITY SET is authoritative and the numeric count
   six is NOT (R2's "six keys" is demoted to a description); dm-adjudicator is DISTINCT from
   campaign-ruling, carried by an explicit boundaryKind ('designed-adjudication' vs
   'source-ambiguity'); the probabilistic Wish transition EXECUTES in the seeded reference
   harness and emits a durable state-transition RESULT without requiring persistence
   storage; NO speculative LedgerMigration bead now (R2 Q7 withdrawn).

=== R3's ONE UNRESOLVED QUESTION NOW HAS AN OWNER 2026-07-28 ===
R3 item 2 recorded that "the eshyra-review-checkpoint mechanism does not exist
yet, and F1 is forbidden from building it", leaving open whether F1-A may merge
on a fixture or must wait for the durable mechanism.

The mechanism is now built: eshyra-o9bd.19.1.17, protocol eshyra-review-v2,
PR #481 (open, unmerged, awaiting a manual full semantic-system review). This
bead now DEPENDS on it. F1 does not start until #481 merges.

WHAT F1 CONSUMES, and how it differs from R3's sketch:
- Checkpoint kinds are SPLIT. R3 described one binding; the shipped model has
  contract-authorization {reviewedScope, publicationHeadSha, reviewerRole,
  result, implementationPermission} and implementation-review {reviewedHeadSha,
  reviewMode, result, ...}. F1's gate is the AUTHORIZATION kind: it answers "may
  this contract be implemented", which is what F1 actually asked for.
- R3's procedureIds[] is NOT a checkpoint field. Authorization is all-or-nothing
  over the whole contract: reviewedScope 'partial' grants nothing, and granting
  permission on partial scope is a rejected contradiction. R3 wanted
  per-procedure review PLUS integrated full-contract-hash approval; per-procedure
  granularity therefore lives in the CONTRACT (scope fields), and the checkpoint
  approves the contract hash. F1 should re-derive its five REVIEW_CHECKPOINT_*
  failure codes against this shape:
    _MISSING           -> no valid contract-authorization checkpoint
    _CONTRACT_MISMATCH -> identityDrift() reports 'normalized contract changed'
    _SCOPE_GAP         -> reviewedScope !== 'full-contract'
    _PERMISSION_DENIED -> implementationPermission !== 'granted'
    _HEAD_DRIFT        -> DOES NOT APPLY to authorization. Deliberate: later
                          implementation commits do not invalidate an
                          authorization while contract/profile/policy hashes are
                          unchanged. Head freshness binds IMPLEMENTATION review.
- R3's contractHash (JCS over the F1 ledger contract) and the review system's
  contractHash (JCS over the normalized bead REVIEW CONTRACT) are DIFFERENT
  HASHES OVER DIFFERENT ARTIFACTS. F1 must not conflate them. The review
  checkpoint approves the bead contract; APPROVED_CONTRACT_HASH still gates F1's
  own ledger bytes. R3 item 2's point stands and is now stated in the protocol
  doc: a matching hash constant proves bytes are unchanged, never that a review
  occurred.
- FIXTURE ISOLATION IS ENFORCED, answering the sequencing question in the
  restrictive direction: a fixture checkpoint cannot authorize a real PR, bead,
  or contract, under any environment variable or path. F1-A may be BUILT against
  packages/core/test/fixtures/review/, but it cannot be DECLARED APPROVED that
  way. F1-A needs a real contract-authorization checkpoint before merge.

F1's declared profile is rules-clause-complete, which also requires the
semantic-system sections (strictness is cumulative). Its contract must be
written into this bead as a single normative "## REVIEW CONTRACT" block; run
npm run review:preflight -- --bead eshyra-o9bd.19.1.14 to validate it before
requesting authorization. No F1 implementation was started in this session.
